criteria.reason: Sudden painless monocular vision loss persisting for two hours requires immediate emergency eye and vascular assessment. The draft directs ED attendance now without waiting; no unresolved prerequisite delays that assessment.

Immediate emergency assessment is proportionate to possible retinal arterial occlusion or retinal detachment. Messaging or routine outpatient review cannot meet the time-sensitive examination requirement. The draft avoids mandatory ambulance transport while prohibiting self-driving.

Onset, persistence, laterality, pain denial and age are grounded in the original message. Diagnoses remain possibilities, and neurological symptoms, headache, jaw symptoms and measurements are explicitly unknown rather than inferred.

Supplied passages support CRAO as a time-critical stroke equivalent, curtain-like loss as a retinal-detachment presentation, and consideration of arteritic occlusion over age 50. The draft acknowledges source limitations and diagnostic uncertainty.
New weakness or speech difficulty triggers immediate 911 activation, independently of the existing instruction to attend the ED now. The patient is advised not to drive.
No question is issued and emergency attendance is not contingent on further history or measurements.
The draft directs care to an emergency department without claiming booking, acceptance, coordination or a response guarantee.

transportReview.draftQuote: Go to an emergency department now — do not wait.
